# QAccelPlot

QAccelPlot is a 2D plotting library for Qt Quick. Curves render through the Qt
Scene Graph with GPU shaders, and C++ data paths replace large data sets every
frame.

### Key capabilities

- **Throughput** — about 8M points replaced and drawn per frame at 60 FPS on the
  [reference system](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance-comparison/), without downsampling
- **Data paths** — QML points, double vectors, moved `float` buffers, and
  worker-thread `postData()`
- **Interaction** — pan, cursor-centered, per-axis, and rectangle zoom, rescale,
  hover hit testing, and plot mouse events for custom tools
- **Inspection** — crosshair, tooltip, nearest-data-point queries, and region
  selection with statistics
- **Invalid data points** — `NaN`, `±Inf`, and non-positive log values break or
  connect the curve consistently
- **Curves** — solid, dashed, and marker-only styles; gradient fills and
  strokes; morph and draw transitions
- **Point clouds** — `PointCloud` for large scatter data, colored uniformly or
  by value, with a `ColorBar`
- **Heatmaps** — `HeatmapSeries` for grids of values colored through a
  colormap
- **Bars** — `BarSeries` for vertical, horizontal, and grouped bar charts
- **Histograms** — `Histogram` counts samples into equal or uneven bins, as
  counts or density
- **Bands** — `BandSeries` for confidence intervals and envelopes
- **Error bars** — `ErrorBarSeries` for symmetric and asymmetric errors,
  vertical or horizontal
- **Layout** — secondary and extra axes, data-anchored QML overlays, and
  `RectangleSeries` for event spans and state timelines

### Quick start

```qml
import QtQuick
import QAccelPlot as QAccelPlot

QAccelPlot.Plot {
    id: plot
    anchors.fill: parent
    xAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis { viewportMin: 0; viewportMax: 10 }
    yAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis { viewportMin: -1; viewportMax: 1 }
    QAccelPlot.LineCurve { xAxis: plot.xAxis; yAxis: plot.yAxis; color: "steelblue" }
}
```

See [Getting started](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/getting-started/) for the full build and data setup.

Each recipe links to a complete, runnable
[example](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples).

## Requirements

- CMake 3.16 or newer
- A C++17 compiler
- Qt 6.2 or newer with Core, Gui, Quick, and ShaderTools
- A hardware Qt Quick Scene Graph backend

QAccelPlot builds as a static library. Qt's `QuickPrivate` component is
optional; see
[texture upload modes](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/#select-the-texture-upload-mode).

## Licensing

GPLv3 with the Universal FOSS Exception, or a commercial license. See
[`LICENSING.md`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/blob/main/LICENSING.md).
Qt is licensed separately.

# Getting started

Project layout:

```text
my-plot-app/
├── CMakeLists.txt
├── main.cpp
└── qml/
    └── Main.qml
```

## 1. Add QAccelPlot to the build

Create `CMakeLists.txt`:

```cmake
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)

project(MyPlotApp VERSION 1.0 LANGUAGES CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

find_package(Qt6 6.2 REQUIRED COMPONENTS Core Gui Quick ShaderTools)

include(FetchContent)
FetchContent_Declare(
    QAccelPlot
    GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot.git
    GIT_TAG v0.4.0
)
FetchContent_MakeAvailable(QAccelPlot)

qt_add_executable(MyPlotApp MANUAL_FINALIZATION
    main.cpp
)

set_source_files_properties(qml/Main.qml PROPERTIES QT_RESOURCE_ALIAS Main.qml)
qt_add_resources(MyPlotApp "app_qml"
    PREFIX "/app"
    FILES qml/Main.qml
)

target_link_libraries(MyPlotApp PRIVATE
    Qt6::Core
    Qt6::Gui
    Qt6::Quick
    QAccelPlot::QAccelPlot
)

qt_import_qml_plugins(MyPlotApp)
qt_finalize_executable(MyPlotApp)
```

- `QAccelPlot::QAccelPlot` links the library and its static QML plugin.
  `qt_import_qml_plugins()` must run before `qt_finalize_executable()`.
- `ShaderTools` compiles the curve shaders at build time.
- As a subproject, QAccelPlot's examples, tests, benchmarks, and install rules
  default to off.

??? note "Windows: launching from Explorer"

    Windows has no build RPATH. To start the application outside the IDE,
    deploy the Qt runtime beside it by appending:

    ```cmake
    if(WIN32)
        find_program(MY_PLOT_APP_WINDEPLOYQT
            NAMES windeployqt
            HINTS "${Qt6_DIR}/../../../bin"
            REQUIRED
        )

        add_custom_command(TARGET MyPlotApp POST_BUILD
            COMMAND "${MY_PLOT_APP_WINDEPLOYQT}"
                --qmldir "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/qml"
                --no-translations
                "$<TARGET_FILE:MyPlotApp>"
            COMMENT "Deploying the Qt runtime beside MyPlotApp"
            VERBATIM
        )
    endif()
    ```

To use a local checkout, replace the `FetchContent` block with:

```cmake
add_subdirectory(path/to/QAccelPlot ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/QAccelPlot)
```

The second argument is required when the checkout is outside the application's
source tree.

## 2. Create the plot

Create `qml/Main.qml`:

```qml
import QtQuick
import QAccelPlot as QAccelPlot

Window {
    width: 800
    height: 500
    visible: true
    title: "QAccelPlot example"

    QAccelPlot.Plot {
        id: plot
        anchors.fill: parent
        legendVisible: false

        xAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {
            viewportMin: 0
            viewportMax: 10
            label: "Time (s)"
        }

        yAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {
            viewportMin: -1.2
            viewportMax: 1.2
            label: "Amplitude"
            labelPadding: 34
        }

        QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
            objectName: "curve"
            xAxis: plot.xAxis
            yAxis: plot.yAxis
            color: QAccelPlot.Colors.dark.seriesPrimary
            lineWidth: 2
        }
    }
}
```

Every series needs an X and a Y axis. [`viewportMin`][viewport-min] and
[`viewportMax`][viewport-max] set the visible range. A rescale fits the
viewport to the data of the attached series.

## 3. Supply data from C++

Create `main.cpp`:

```cpp
#include <QAccelPlot/series/LineCurve.hpp>

#include <QGuiApplication>
#include <QQmlApplicationEngine>

#include <vector>

int main(int argc, char* argv[])
{
    QGuiApplication app(argc, argv);
    QQmlApplicationEngine engine;
    engine.load(QUrl(QStringLiteral("qrc:/app/Main.qml")));

    auto* root = engine.rootObjects().value(0);
    auto* curve = root
        ? root->findChild<QAccelPlot::LineCurve*>(QStringLiteral("curve"))
        : nullptr;
    if (!curve) {
        return -1;
    }

    const std::vector<double> times { 0, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10 };
    const std::vector<double> amplitudes { 0, 0.8, -0.6, 0.4, 0 };
    curve->setData(times, amplitudes);
    return app.exec();
}
```

Public headers are included with the `QAccelPlot/` prefix, for example
`<QAccelPlot/series/LineCurve.hpp>`.

[`setData()`][set-data-vectors] takes separate X and Y vectors and suits small,
static data. For large or streaming data, see the
[Performance guide](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/#select-the-data-path).

## 4. Configure and build

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --config Release
```

Add `-DQACCELPLOT_USE_QT_PRIVATE_API=OFF` when private Qt headers are not
installed; see
[texture upload modes](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/#select-the-texture-upload-mode).

## Default interaction

- Drag inside the plot area to pan all attached axes.
- Use the mouse wheel over the plot to zoom all axes around the mouse pointer.
- Use the mouse wheel over an individual axis to zoom only that axis.
- Enable `rectangleZoom.enabled` for Ctrl + left drag rectangle zoom.
  See [Rectangle zoom](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/rectangle-zoom/).
- Double-click the plot to rescale all axes to their data ranges.
- Double-click an axis to rescale that axis only.

See [Troubleshooting](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/troubleshooting/) for common setup issues.

[viewport-min]: api/classQAccelPlot_1_1Axis.md#property-viewportmin-12
[viewport-max]: api/classQAccelPlot_1_1Axis.md#property-viewportmax-12
[set-data-vectors]: api/classQAccelPlot_1_1LineCurve.md#function-setdata-28

# Concepts and architecture

![QAccelPlot architecture](assets/architecture.svg)

## Plot and PlotView

`PlotView` is the C++ plot item. It lays out axes, converts between data and
pixel coordinates, handles pan and zoom, and collects child series.

`Plot` is the QML wrapper most applications use. It adds a `Legend`,
`legendModel`, and `legendVisible` to the full `PlotView` interface.

[`plotRect`][plot-rect] is the data area, excluding axes and padding. Use it to
place clipped overlays and custom tools.

## Axes and ranges

An `Axis` has two related ranges:

- The **viewport range** ([`viewportMin`][viewport-min], [`viewportMax`][viewport-max]) is visible.
- The **data range** ([`dataMin`][data-min], [`dataMax`][data-max]) is the extent reported by
  attached series.

Panning and zooming change the viewport. [`rescaleToData()`][rescale-to-data]
sets the viewport to fit the data range, and [`autoRescale`][auto-rescale]
does so on every data update. A series reports its extent to the
axes set in its [`xAxis`][series-x-axis] and [`yAxis`][series-y-axis] properties.
The extent is
[computed on demand](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/#data-ranges-are-computed-on-demand).

| Plot property | Side |
| --- | --- |
| [`xAxis`][plot-x-axis] | Bottom |
| [`x2Axis`][plot-x2-axis] | Top |
| [`yAxis`][plot-y-axis] | Left |
| [`y2Axis`][plot-y2-axis] | Right |
| [`extraAxes`][extra-axes] | Set by each axis's `side` |

Each series selects its own axes.

`AxisTicker` controls tick count, subticks, lengths, colors, fonts, rotation,
and label formatting. Built-in formatters cover numeric, date/time,
logarithmic, and categorical labels; `TickLabelFormatter` also accepts a
JavaScript callback.

## Series

`PlotSeries` holds properties shared by all series: name, axes, plot rectangle,
legend symbol, and `hoverEnabled`. `legendEntry()` describes how a legend draws the series;
`LegendModel` lists the entries of the visible series that have one. Only the
topmost series under the mouse pointer is hovered; `hoverEnabled: false` leaves
hover to the series beneath.

`LineCurve` renders lines, markers, line styles, gradients, and fills. It
accepts data from QML or C++ buffers, as doubles or as interleaved floats.
It reports `hovered` within `hoverRadius` pixels of the line or over a marker.
Set `hoverRadius: 0` on a line drawn over another series to leave hover to the
series beneath.

`PointCloud` renders unconnected points as markers, colored uniformly or by a
per-point value through a `Colormap`. It reports the hovered point index.

`HeatmapSeries` renders a uniform grid of values as cells colored through a
`Colormap`, placed by the outer edges of the grid. `PointCloud` and
`HeatmapSeries` derive from `ColormappedSeries`, which resolves the value range
that a `ColorBar` shows.

`BandSeries` fills the area between a low and a high value at each X, such as
confidence intervals and envelopes. It stores `(x, low, high)` triples and
can draw lines along both edges.

`ErrorBarSeries` draws a capped line from a low to a high bound at each data
point, along the Y axis or, with `orientation: Qt.Horizontal`, the X axis. It
stores `(x, y, low, high)` quadruples and does not draw the values.

`RectangleSeries` renders many data-space rectangles in one item, such as event
spans and state timelines. Infinite edges reach the plot edge, and a
per-rectangle category selects the fill color. It reports the hovered
rectangle index.

`BarSeries` renders bar charts from (position, value) pairs. `barWidth`,
`barOffset`, and `baselineValue` shape the bars in the shader, and
`orientation` selects vertical or horizontal bars. Ranged bars carry their
own extent as (from, to, value), e.g. the bins of a histogram.

## Invalid data points and gaps

`LineCurve` applies one invalid-data-point contract to rendering, gradient fills,
dash patterns, transitions, auto-ranging, and hover hit testing. For the other
series, see [bands](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/bands/#invalid-data-points),
[error bars](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/error-bars/#invalid-data-points),
[point clouds](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/point-clouds/#invalid-points), and
[bars](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/bar-charts/#invalid-bars).

A data point is **invalid** when its X or Y coordinate is `NaN` or `±Inf`, or when a
coordinate is zero or negative on a logarithmic axis. Mark missing data by
inserting a data point with a `NaN` coordinate. JavaScript `null` and `undefined`
are not gap markers.

Gap rendering is configured through the curve's [`gaps`][line-curve] grouped
property. `gaps.nanMode` selects how the line and fill treat invalid data points:

```qml
QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
    gaps.nanMode: QAccelPlot.NanGapMode.Connect
}
```

| `gaps.nanMode` | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `NanGapMode.Break` (default) | No segment or fill is drawn to or from an invalid data point. Valid neighbors end squarely, and a valid data point isolated between two invalid data points draws no line. With a [step mode](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/styling/#step-lines), a value still holds up to the X of an invalid neighbor when that X is finite. |
| `NanGapMode.Connect` | Invalid data points are skipped and the line, fill, and hit test join the nearest valid data points. |

Despite its name, `nanMode` applies to every invalid data point, including `±Inf`
and non-positive log-axis values.

In both modes:

- **Markers** are never drawn for invalid data points.
- **Auto-ranging** judges each coordinate on its own. A data point with a valid X
  and an invalid Y still extends the X range, so a dropout keeps its timestamp.
  If a dimension has no valid coordinate, the series clears that range.
- **Dash patterns** continue across a gap; the gap contributes no dash length.
- **`MorphTransition`** shows a data point that becomes invalid as a gap
  immediately, and a data point that becomes valid jumps to its target instead of
  animating from `NaN`.
- **Hover** never reports a hit on an invalid data point or across a break.

## Composition and overlays

Ordinary QML items can be placed above the grid and series. `DataAnchor` maps
one or two data coordinates to a QML item's geometry, so labels, event lines,
regions, and drag handles follow the data while panning and zooming.

For custom tools, `PlotView` provides [`dataToPixelX()`][data-to-pixel-x],
[`dataToPixelY()`][data-to-pixel-y], [`pixelToDataX()`][pixel-to-data-x],
[`pixelToDataY()`][pixel-to-data-y], and [`isInsidePlotArea()`][is-inside-plot-area].
Accepting a plot mouse event suppresses the default pan.

## Rendering and threads

QML objects and setters run on the UI thread; Qt synchronizes their state to
the Scene Graph render thread. Curve renderers keep persistent Scene Graph
nodes and use precompiled shaders for the active graphics API. The software
backend cannot run these shaders.

Produce data on a worker thread if needed, but never mutate UI objects from it.
Use [`LineCurve::postData()`][post-data] or a queued call. See
[Background data production](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/background-data/).

[data-max]: api/classQAccelPlot_1_1Axis.md#property-datamax-12

# Performance

Throughput depends on point count, update rate, data conversion, range scans,
series count, line style, effects, window size, graphics backend, and refresh
rate. Measure a workload that matches your application. For cross-library
numbers, see the [performance comparison](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance-comparison/).

## Select the data path

| API | Use it when | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`setData(QList<QPointF>)`][set-data-points] | Data originates in QML | Allocation and interleaving |
| [`setData(xs, ys)`][set-data-vectors] | C++ data is in separate double vectors | Allocation and interleaving |
| [`setData(std::vector<double>&&, count)`][set-data-moved] | C++ data is interleaved doubles | Moved, no copy |
| [`setDataF(const float*, count)`][set-data-f-copy] | Interleaved floats stay caller-owned | One copy into a reusable buffer |
| [`setDataF(std::vector<float>&&, count)`][set-data-f-moved] | Interleaved floats, on the curve's thread | Moved, no copy |
| `postData()` with a [float][post-data] or [double][post-data-double] vector | A worker thread owns the completed buffer | Queues the moved-buffer handoff |

Start with [`setDataF(std::vector<float>&&, count)`][set-data-f-moved] for large
C++ data sets.

Use a [`setData()`][set-data-points] overload for Unix-epoch timestamps, large
coordinates, or small differences at a large offset. These paths keep doubles
and rebase the GPU buffer so nearby values stay distinct. The `F` APIs store
floats.

The table shows `LineCurve`. Every series has `setData()`,
`setDataF()`, and `postData()` overloads for its own record layout.

[`setDataFWithCache()`][set-data-f-with-cache] also accepts a
prebuilt vertex cache, so vertex assembly can move off the UI and render
threads. It ties application code to renderer details; use it only when
measurements justify it. The cache must match the current point count and
renderer layout, otherwise it is rejected and normal vertex assembly runs. For
a step line, build it with `buildVertexCache(data, count, cache, stepMode)`.

## Data ranges are computed on demand

No setter scans the data for its range. After an update, a series scans its
records the first time something reads the range:

| Reader | Scans |
| --- | --- |
| [`rescaleToData()`][rescale-to-data], `rescaleAllAxes()`, a double-click | Once per call |
| An axis with [`autoRescale`][auto-rescale] | On every data update |
| [`dataMin`][data-min] / [`dataMax`][data-max], or a binding to them | On every data update that is followed by a read |
| A `LineCurve` gradient with a `DataRange` bound | On every data update of that curve |

[`appendData()`][append-data] widens a computed range without a rescan.

To skip the scan when the extents are already known, pass them with the data:

```cpp
const auto bounds = QAccelPlot::PlotSeries::DataBounds{xMin, xMax, yMin, yMax};
curve->setDataF(std::move(points), pointCount, bounds);
```

The bounds describe that update only. A change that affects which values are
valid, such as switching an axis to a logarithmic scale, discards them.

## Build buffers efficiently

- For the `F` paths, store points as interleaved floats: `[x0, y0, x1, y1, ...]`.
- Reserve or resize the vector once before filling it.
- Move the completed vector instead of copying it.
- Publish no faster than the display presents frames.
- For a fixed streaming window, pass the window's bounds with each frame, as in
  the [`realtime` example](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/data/realtime).

## Keep work off the UI thread

Generate data on a worker thread and hand off only completed buffers, using
[`postData()`][post-data] or a queued call. Never write to a `QQuickItem` from
the worker. If producers are faster than the display, keep at most one pending
batch; see [Background data production](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/background-data/).

## Optional rendering costs

### Hover interactions

Hover cost per mouse move:

| Series | Cost |
| --- | --- |
| `LineCurve` | Checks one bounding box per 512 points, then the segments and markers in the matching boxes. `hoverRadius: 0` skips the segments. |
| `PointCloud`, `RectangleSeries` | Tests every record, roughly 1–2 ms per million, until those scans have cost as much as a spatial index. The index is then built, and later moves test only nearby records. Data replaced every frame never builds one. |
| `BarSeries` | Builds a grid on the first move after a data change, then tests nearby bars. |

A `RectangleSeries` also tests every rectangle spanning more than 64 grid
cells, so many long rectangles make its lookup `O(N)`.

Set `hoverEnabled: false` to turn hover off for one series. Set the environment
variable `QACCELPLOT_HOVER_ENABLED=0` to turn it off for every series and axis,
for example in streaming-only views.

### Other rendering costs

- Markers add geometry and fragment work per visible point. Fragment work grows
  with marker size; `LineCurve.Pixel` markers shade one pixel per point and
  suit very dense scatter plots.
- A `PointCloud` or `HeatmapSeries` whose `Colormap` leaves `min` or `max` unset scans every value
  on each data update to resolve the range. Set both when the bounds of
  streaming values are known.
- Gradient effects add material and domain work.
- Transitions update intermediate data while animating.
- Many series add per-node and per-material overhead at the same total point
  count.
- Larger windows and high-DPI displays add fragment work.

Changing line width, marker size, or color is cheaper than changing data, but
still schedules a redraw.

## Use a hardware backend

Curves require a hardware Qt Quick Scene Graph backend: OpenGL, OpenGL ES,
Direct3D 11/12, Vulkan, or Metal. The software backend skips curve rendering and
emits a warning. When a curve is blank or slow, check `QSG_RHI_BACKEND`,
`QT_QUICK_BACKEND`, remote-desktop sessions, and GPU drivers.

## Select the texture upload mode

Curve coordinates live in a GPU data texture. How live updates reach it depends
on `QACCELPLOT_USE_QT_PRIVATE_API`:

| Mode | Upload | Use when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ON` (default when `Qt6::QuickPrivate` is found) | `QSGPlainTexture::setImage()` replaces the texture contents in place | Large data sets updated every frame |
| `OFF` | `QQuickWindow::createTextureFromImage()` recreates the texture | Private Qt dependencies are unacceptable for packaging |

No private Qt types appear in public headers or ABI. Gradient textures always
use the public path.

Benchmark both modes with your workload, or configure the
[included benchmarks](#included-benchmarks) once with each value.

## Benchmarking

- Build QAccelPlot and the application in Release mode, and warm up shaders,
  allocations, and caches before recording.
- Record presented frames ([`QQuickWindow::frameSwapped`][frame-swapped]), not
  timer callbacks, and report the frame-time distribution as well as the
  average.
- For streamed data, also report how many new datasets are applied per second:
  several presented frames can show the same dataset.
- Record the Qt version, OS, GPU, driver, graphics API, resolution, and device
  pixel ratio with the result.

### Performance Lab

[`examples/showcases/performance`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/showcases/performance)
streams a `LineCurve`, a `PointCloud`, a `RectangleSeries`, a `BarSeries`, and
a `HeatmapSeries`, one per tab, with options for record and series count, ingestion API, hover,
and rendering. Change one option at a time, at a record count that keeps
display FPS below the refresh rate. The lab reports:

- **Display FPS** — frames presented to the screen.
- **Data Update Rate** (Hz) — new datasets applied to the plot per second,
  including worker-side generation.
- **Peak update gap** — the longest interval between two dataset applications
  in the last reporting period.
- **Throughput** — points, rectangles, bars, or heatmap cells updated per
  second.

### Included benchmarks

- Frame time runs from just before the data or viewport update until
  `QQuickRenderControl::endFrame()` returns: data copy, scene-graph sync,
  texture staging, rendering, command submission, and GPU completion. Data
  generation is excluded.
- Live scenarios cover 1M, 2M, 5M, and 10M points; static scenarios
  pan the viewport over one fixed buffer.
- Multi-curve throughput counts points across all curves.
- Separate executables measure CPU ingestion and vertex-cache building without
  rendering.

Build them with:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DQACCELPLOT_BUILD_BENCHMARKS=ON \
  -DQACCELPLOT_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF \
  -DQACCELPLOT_BUILD_TESTS=OFF
cmake --build build --config Release
```

Scenarios are defined in
[`benchmarks/common/BenchmarkScenario.cpp`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/blob/main/benchmarks/common/BenchmarkScenario.cpp).

[set-data-f-copy]: api/classQAccelPlot_1_1LineCurve.md#function-setdataf-16

<!-- source: docs/guide/faq.md -->

# FAQ

## How does QAccelPlot differ from QCustomPlot or Qt Graphs?

| | QAccelPlot | Qt Graphs | QCustomPlot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UI framework | Qt Quick | Qt Quick | Qt Widgets |
| Rendering | Custom Scene Graph shaders | Qt Scene Graph | `QPainter`, optional OpenGL |
| Points replaced per frame at 60 FPS\* | ~8M | ~13K | ~2.75M (OpenGL) |

\* Single curve on the [reference system](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance-comparison/).

## How many data points can QAccelPlot handle?

About 8M points replaced and drawn every frame at 60 FPS on the
[reference system](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance-comparison/). Throughput drops with more
series, markers, gradients, transitions, larger windows, and slower GPUs.
Measure your workload with the included
[benchmarks](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/benchmarks).

## What is the fastest way to supply data?

Move an interleaved float buffer with
[`setDataF(std::vector<float>&&, int)`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1LineCurve/#function-setdataf-26).
See [Select the data path](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/#select-the-data-path).

## Is QAccelPlot thread-safe?

No. Access QML objects and properties, including `setDataF()`, on the UI
thread. Produce data on any thread and hand it off through
[`postData()`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1LineCurve/#function-postdata-22) or a
queued call. See [Background data production](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/background-data/).

## Which Qt versions are supported?

Qt 6.2 or newer with Core, Gui, Quick, and ShaderTools. `QuickPrivate` is
optional; see
[texture upload modes](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/#select-the-texture-upload-mode).

## What graphics backends does QAccelPlot support?

OpenGL, OpenGL ES, Direct3D 11/12, Vulkan, and Metal. The software backend
cannot run the curve shaders; see
[The axes appear but the curve is blank](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/troubleshooting/#the-axes-appear-but-the-curve-is-blank).

## Does QAccelPlot work with Qt Widgets?

Only through `QQuickWidget`. There is no `QWidget`-based API.

## What licenses are available?

- **GPLv3 with the Universal FOSS Exception** — free for applications
  distributed under an OSI-approved or FSF-free license.
- **Commercial** — for proprietary or closed-source distribution. Contact
  [qaccelplot@gmail.com](mailto:qaccelplot@gmail.com).

See [LICENSING.md](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/blob/main/LICENSING.md).


---

<!-- source: docs/guide/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

## `module "QAccelPlot" is not installed`

QAccelPlot is a static QML module. Check that the application:

- links `QAccelPlot::QAccelPlot`,
- calls `qt_import_qml_plugins()` before `qt_finalize_executable()`,
- imports `QAccelPlot` in QML.

See the CMake file in [Getting started](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/getting-started/). Delete the
application build directory after changing plugin linkage; stale generated
import files can hide the fix.

## CMake cannot find `QuickPrivate`

`QACCELPLOT_USE_QT_PRIVATE_API=ON` requires `Qt6::QuickPrivate`. Qt 6.11 and
newer package it as a separate component. Install the private development
package for the exact Qt build, and check `Qt6_DIR`, `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, the
compiler architecture, and the Qt version reported during configuration. A
package from a different Qt patch release, compiler, or architecture does not
work.

To build without it:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DQACCELPLOT_USE_QT_PRIVATE_API=OFF
```

This is slower for large data sets updated every frame; see
[texture upload modes](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/#select-the-texture-upload-mode).

## The axes appear but the curve is blank

Check these conditions:

1. The `LineCurve` has both [`xAxis`][series-x-axis] and [`yAxis`][series-y-axis] assigned.
2. At least two points exist when a line is enabled, or one point when only a
   marker is enabled.
3. The viewport includes the point coordinates.
4. The Qt Quick renderer is not using the software backend: QAccelPlot logs a
   warning when it is. Check `QSG_RHI_BACKEND` and `QT_QUICK_BACKEND`.
5. The data buffer contains exactly two floats per declared point.

## Rescale does not fit the data

Data passed with `DataBounds` is not scanned: a rescale fits the given bounds,
so they must cover the data. Every series attached to an axis contributes to
its data range.

## Pan and zoom snap back

An axis with [`autoRescale`][auto-rescale] refits its viewport on every
data update. Set `autoRescale` to `false` while the user navigates.

## A real-time plot stutters

- Run the data producer off the UI thread.
- Use a Release build.
- Move interleaved float buffers instead of building `QList<QPointF>`.
- Do not publish more frames than the display presents.
- Disable markers, gradients, and transitions to isolate rendering cost.
- Measure [`frameSwapped`][frame-swapped] intervals and producer throughput separately.

See the [Performance guide](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/) and
[Background data production](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/background-data/).

## Reporting a problem

Include:

- A minimal reproducer or the closest included example.
- QAccelPlot version.
- Qt version and installation source.
- OS, compiler, architecture, GPU, and driver.
- Active Qt Quick graphics API.
- Release or Debug configuration.
- Logs, screenshots, or benchmark JSON where relevant.

Report through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/issues).

[series-x-axis]: api/classQAccelPlot_1_1PlotSeries.md#property-xaxis-12
[series-y-axis]: api/classQAccelPlot_1_1PlotSeries.md#property-yaxis-12
[auto-rescale]: api/classQAccelPlot_1_1Axis.md#property-autorescale-12
[frame-swapped]: https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qquickwindow.html#frameSwapped

<!-- source: docs/guide/cookbook/basic-plot.md -->

# Basic static plot

A `Plot` needs axes and one or more series. Each series names the axes that map
its data and optionally supplies a `name` for the legend.

```qml
import QtQuick
import QAccelPlot as QAccelPlot

QAccelPlot.Plot {
    id: plot

    xAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {
        viewportMin: 0
        viewportMax: 24
        label: "Time of day (h)"
    }

    yAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {
        viewportMin: 16
        viewportMax: 27
        label: "Temperature (°C)"
    }

    QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
        name: "Measured"
        xAxis: plot.xAxis
        yAxis: plot.yAxis
        color: "tomato"
        lineWidth: 3
        Component.onCompleted: setData([
            Qt.point(0, 18), Qt.point(6, 19.5),
            Qt.point(12, 25), Qt.point(18, 23.5), Qt.point(24, 18)
        ])
    }

    QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
        name: "Forecast"
        xAxis: plot.xAxis
        yAxis: plot.yAxis
        color: "dodgerblue"
        lineWidth: 2
        lineStyle: QAccelPlot.DashLine { pattern: [8, 5] }
        marker.shape: QAccelPlot.LineCurve.Diamond
        marker.size: 7
    }
}
```

`Plot` shows a legend entry for every visible series that has one; a heatmap
has none, because its color bar is its key. Set `legendVisible: false` to hide
the legend, or assign `legend` to replace it. `Plot.legendModel` lists every
entry; a `LegendModel` of your own lists a subset:

```qml
legend: QAccelPlot.Legend {
    model: QAccelPlot.LegendModel { series: [measured, fit] }
}
```

QML [`setData()`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1LineCurve/#function-setdata-18)
suits small or rarely changing data. For large or frequent updates, see
[Select the data path](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/#select-the-data-path).

Complete source: [`examples/quickstart`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/quickstart)


---

<!-- source: docs/guide/cookbook/realtime.md -->

# Real-time scrolling data

Keep the viewport fixed and replace the visible buffer once per frame.

## Declare a stable viewport

```qml
import QtQuick
import QAccelPlot as QAccelPlot

QAccelPlot.Plot {
    id: plot

    xAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {
        viewportMin: -20
        viewportMax: 0
        label: "Time before present (s)"
    }

    yAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {
        viewportMin: -2.5
        viewportMax: 2.5
        label: "Acceleration (g)"
    }

    QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
        objectName: "vibrationCurve"
        xAxis: plot.xAxis
        yAxis: plot.yAxis
        lineWidth: 2.5
    }
}
```

## Update every frame

Pass each new buffer to [`setDataF()`][set-data-f]:

```cpp
curve->setDataF(std::move(points), pointCount);
```

A rescale fits the data points of the current frame. To fit the nominal window
instead, pass its bounds with the data. This also skips the
[range scan](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/#data-ranges-are-computed-on-demand):

```cpp
constexpr auto bounds = QAccelPlot::PlotSeries::DataBounds{-20.0, 0.0, -2.5, 2.5};
curve->setDataF(std::move(points), pointCount, bounds);
```

If buffer generation is expensive, move it to a worker thread; see
[Background data production](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/background-data/).

## Follow the data range

To fit an axis to the data instead of fixing its viewport, set
[`autoRescale`][auto-rescale]. The viewport is refitted on every data update,
including each [`appendData()`][append-data] call:

```qml
yAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {
    autoRescale: true
}
```

- The fit is exact, as with [`rescaleToData()`][rescale-to-data].
- A panned or zoomed viewport is replaced on the next update. Set
  `autoRescale` to `false` while the user navigates.
- Appending only extends the data range. Replace the buffer with
  [`setDataF()`][set-data-f] to let the range shrink.
- Each update scans the data for its range, unless it appends or passes
  bounds.
- When the last series on the axis is cleared, the viewport is kept.

## Show dropouts as gaps

Write `NaN` for lost or invalid data points instead of repeating or dropping them.
The curve breaks there, and the gap is excluded from auto-ranging and hover:

```cpp
const auto value = packet.valid ? packet.value : std::numeric_limits<float>::quiet_NaN();
points[index * 2] = timestamp;
points[index * 2 + 1] = value;
```

To draw across dropouts instead, set
`gaps.nanMode: QAccelPlot.NanGapMode.Connect`. See
[Invalid data points and gaps](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/concepts/#invalid-data-points-and-gaps).

Complete sources:

- [`examples/data/realtime`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/data/realtime)
- [`examples/data/missing_data`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/data/missing_data)

[set-data-f]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1LineCurve.md#function-setdataf-26
[auto-rescale]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1Axis.md#property-autorescale-12
[append-data]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1LineCurve.md#function-appenddata
[rescale-to-data]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1Axis.md#function-rescaletodata

<!-- source: docs/guide/cookbook/axis-formats.md -->

# Axis formats

Axis values remain numeric. A formatter changes only the displayed tick text.

## Date and time

Use milliseconds since the Unix epoch as X values and attach a
`QAccelPlot.DateTimeTickLabelFormatter`:

```qml
xAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {
    viewportMin: traceStart
    viewportMax: traceEnd

    ticker.tickLabelFormatter: QAccelPlot.DateTimeTickLabelFormatter {
        dateTimeFormat: "hh:mm:ss.zzz"
    }
}
```

Supply epoch values through `setData()`, which keeps double precision; the `F`
APIs store floats.

## Categories

Map integer coordinates to labels with `QAccelPlot.TextTickLabelFormatter`:

```qml
xAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {
    viewportMin: 0
    viewportMax: 6
    ticker.tickCount: 6
    ticker.subtickCount: 0
    ticker.tickLabelFormatter: QAccelPlot.TextTickLabelFormatter {
        labels: ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]
    }
}
```

The data points still use X coordinates `0` through `6`.

## Logarithmic axes

Enable a base-10 logarithmic mapping:

```qml
xAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {
    viewportMin: 20
    viewportMax: 20000
    logScale: true
}
```

Logarithmic ranges must stay positive. The default
`NumericTickLabelFormatter` labels each decade tick as a power of ten, such as
`10⁻³` and `10²`.

## Application-specific labels

For custom text, assign a JavaScript function to a formatter's
[`tickLabel`][tick-label] property. It runs for every tick label, so keep it
cheap:

```qml
yAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {
    viewportMin: 18
    viewportMax: 26
    label: "Temperature"

    ticker.tickLabelFormatter: QAccelPlot.NumericTickLabelFormatter {
        tickLabel: function (temperature) {
            return temperature.toFixed(1) + " °C"
        }
    }
}
```

Complete source: [`examples/axes/tick_formats`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/axes/tick_formats)

[tick-label]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1TickLabelFormatter.md#property-ticklabel-12


---

<!-- source: docs/guide/cookbook/multiple-axes.md -->

# Multiple axes

Each series chooses its own X and Y axes, so several units or sampling domains
can share one plot area.

## Axis layout size

Each axis reserves 50 pixels by default. `layoutSize` sets the height of a
horizontal axis or the width of a vertical axis:

```qml
yAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {
    layoutSize: 90
    label: "Temperature"
}

xAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {
    layoutSize: 70
    label: "Time"
}
```

`layoutSize` does not grow with label text, fonts, or formatters. Choose a value
that fits the tick labels and axis title.

## Secondary axes

[`x2Axis`][x2-axis] is placed at the top and [`y2Axis`][y2-axis] on the right.

```qml
import QtQuick
import QAccelPlot as QAccelPlot

QAccelPlot.Plot {
    id: plot

    xAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {}
    yAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {}
    y2Axis: QAccelPlot.Axis {
        viewportMin: 0
        viewportMax: 100
        label: "Load (%)"
    }

    QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
        xAxis: plot.xAxis
        yAxis: plot.yAxis
    }

    QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
        xAxis: plot.xAxis
        yAxis: plot.y2Axis
    }
}
```

## Extra axes

Use [`extraAxes`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1QAccelPlot/#property-extraaxes-12)
for more than two axes in one orientation. They are laid out in declaration
order: horizontal axes stack below the primary X axis, vertical axes stack from
the plot's left edge inward.

```qml
import QtQuick
import QAccelPlot as QAccelPlot

QAccelPlot.Plot {
    id: plot

    xAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {
        viewportMin: 0
        viewportMax: 10
        label: "Slow time (s)"
    }

    extraAxes: [
        QAccelPlot.Axis {
            id: fastAxis
            orientation: Qt.Horizontal
            side: QAccelPlot.Axis.Bottom
            viewportMin: 0
            viewportMax: 0.5
            label: "Fast time (s)"
        }
    ]

    QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
        xAxis: fastAxis
        yAxis: plot.yAxis
    }
}
```

Complete source: [`examples/axes/multiple_axes`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/axes/multiple_axes)

[x2-axis]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1QAccelPlot.md#property-x2axis-12
[y2-axis]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1QAccelPlot.md#property-y2axis-12


---

<!-- source: docs/guide/cookbook/styling.md -->

# Styling and transitions

## Shared palette

The read-only `Colors` singleton exposes light and dark palettes. Import the
module with an alias to keep `Colors` out of the unqualified namespace:

```qml
import QtQuick
import QAccelPlot as QAccelPlot

QAccelPlot.Plot {
    plotAreaColor: QAccelPlot.Colors.dark.plotArea
    axesAreaColor: QAccelPlot.Colors.dark.axesArea

    QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
        color: QAccelPlot.Colors.dark.seriesPrimary
    }
}
```

Default plot, axis, grid, tick, hover, series, and legend colors come from
`Colors.dark`. Assign `Colors.light` tokens or any colors to restyle a plot.

## Lines and markers

```qml
QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
    color: "dodgerblue"
    lineWidth: 2
    lineStyle: QAccelPlot.DashLine {
        pattern: [14, 5, 3, 5]
    }
    marker.shape: QAccelPlot.LineCurve.Diamond
    marker.size: 5
    antialiasingEnabled: true
    antialiasingFeather: 1
}
```

Line styles are `QAccelPlot.SolidLine`, `QAccelPlot.DashLine`, and
`QAccelPlot.NoLine`. `NoLine` with a marker shape gives a marker-only series.
Marker settings are grouped under `marker`: `shape`, `size`, `filled`, and
`strokeWidth`.
A dash pattern lists alternating on/off lengths in pixels.

## Step lines

[`stepMode`][step-mode] draws the line as horizontal steps joined by vertical
risers:

```qml
QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
    stepMode: QAccelPlot.StepMode.After
}
```

| `StepMode` | Each value holds |
| --- | --- |
| `None` (default) | Nowhere: straight segments join the data points. |
| `Before` | From the previous data point's X up to its own X. |
| `After` | From its own X up to the next data point's X. |
| `Center` | Between the midpoints to its neighbors, halfway on screen (the geometric mean on a log axis). |

- The line starts at the first data point and ends at the last one. To hold the
  last value until now, append a data point at the current X.
- The gradient fill, dash pattern, and hover follow the steps. Markers stay on
  the data points.
- With [`PlotInspector.interpolate`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/data-inspection/), a crosshair between
  two data points reads the value the step holds, and `index` is the data point
  holding it.
- The line follows the data points in order; X is not sorted.

To outline a histogram, repeat the last value at the last edge and draw it with
`After`:

```qml
QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
    stepMode: QAccelPlot.StepMode.After
    Component.onCompleted: {
        const histogram = QAccelPlot.Histogram.fromSamples(samples, 40);
        const values = histogram.values;
        setData(histogram.edges.map((edge, i) => Qt.point(edge, values[Math.min(i, values.length - 1)])));
    }
}
```

## Marker shapes

`marker.size` is the marker radius in pixels. Every shape fits within a square
of that half-width.

| Group | `MarkerShape` values |
| --- | --- |
| Filled shapes | `Circle`, `Square`, `Diamond`, `TriangleUp`, `TriangleDown`, `TriangleLeft`, `TriangleRight`, `Pentagon`, `Hexagon`, `Star` |
| Line shapes | `Cross` (+), `XCross` (×), `Asterisk`, `HLine`, `VLine` |
| Single pixel | `Pixel` |

Set `marker.filled: false` to draw filled shapes as outlines of
`marker.strokeWidth` pixels. The outline lies inside the shape's edge, so hollow
and filled markers have the same size. Line shapes and `Pixel` ignore both
properties.

```qml
QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
    lineStyle: QAccelPlot.NoLine {}
    marker.shape: QAccelPlot.LineCurve.Circle
    marker.size: 4
    marker.filled: false
    marker.strokeWidth: 1
}
```

`Pixel` draws each data point as one logical pixel and ignores `marker.size` and
anti-aliasing. Use it with a semi-transparent color for scatter plots with
hundreds of thousands of points, where overlapping points build up density.
Hover still detects a `Pixel` marker within 3 px.

## Gradient stroke and fill

Effects are attached through the curve's [`effects`][effects] property:

```qml
QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
    effects: [
        QAccelPlot.GradientFill {
            direction: Qt.Vertical
            baseline: QAccelPlot.GradientFillBaseline.Value
            baselineValue: 0
            valueMinSource: QAccelPlot.GradientValueSource.Fixed
            valueMin: -4
            valueMaxSource: QAccelPlot.GradientValueSource.Fixed
            valueMax: 8
            opacity: 0.65
            colormap: QAccelPlot.Colormap { preset: QAccelPlot.Colormap.Viridis }
        }
    ]
}
```

Both effects take their color stops from one of two properties:

- `colormap`: a [`Colormap`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/point-clouds/#color-points-by-value) preset or
  custom ramp. Overrides `gradient` when both are set. Only the ramp is used;
  the colormap's `min`, `max`, and `norm` are ignored.
- `gradient`: a Qt Quick `Gradient`.

```qml
QAccelPlot.GradientStroke {
    gradient: Gradient {
        GradientStop { position: 0; color: "royalblue" }
        GradientStop { position: 1; color: "goldenrod" }
    }
}
```

Fixed gradient bounds keep colors stable while the viewport changes. Axis- or
data-derived bounds make colors follow the current range.

## Animated data changes

Assign a `QAccelPlot.MorphTransition` to [`transition`][transition] to
interpolate from old to new data points, or a `QAccelPlot.DrawTransition` to reveal
the new curve:

```qml
QAccelPlot.MorphTransition {
    id: morph
    duration: 500
    easing.type: Easing.InOutCubic
}

QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
    transition: morph
}
```

Several curves can share one transition; each animates to its own data.
Replacing, clearing, or cancelling `transition`, or calling `appendData()`,
during an animation shows the new data at once.

`BarSeries` and `PointCloud` take the same transitions; see
[bar charts](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/bar-charts/#animate-data-changes) and
[point clouds](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/point-clouds/#animate-data-changes).

Transitions add work on every animated frame. Disable them for continuous
high-rate updates.

Complete sources:

- [`examples/styling/theming`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/styling/theming)
- [`examples/styling/line_styles`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/styling/line_styles)
- [`examples/styling/markers`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/styling/markers)
- [`examples/styling/gradients`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/styling/gradients)
- [`examples/styling/transitions`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/styling/transitions)
- [`examples/plot_types/step_lines`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/plot_types/step_lines)

[effects]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1LineCurve.md#property-effects-12
[step-mode]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1LineCurve.md#property-stepmode-12
[transition]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1LineCurve.md#property-transition-12

<!-- source: docs/guide/cookbook/annotations.md -->

# Annotations and tools

## Attach QML items to data

Place `QAccelPlot.DataAnchor` items in a clipped layer that matches
[`plotRect`][plot-rect]. The layer's origin is the plot area's top-left, so pass
each anchor a local rectangle:

```qml
Item {
    id: annotationLayer
    z: 1
    x: plot.plotRect.x
    y: plot.plotRect.y
    width: plot.plotRect.width
    height: plot.plotRect.height
    clip: true

    QAccelPlot.DataAnchor {
        xAxis: plot.xAxis
        yAxis: plot.yAxis
        plotRect: Qt.rect(0, 0, annotationLayer.width, annotationLayer.height)
        dataX1: 42
        dataY1: plot.yAxis.viewportMin
        dataX2: 42
        dataY2: plot.yAxis.viewportMax

        Rectangle {
            anchors.top: parent.top
            anchors.bottom: parent.bottom
            anchors.horizontalCenter: parent.left
            width: 3
            color: "tomato"
        }
    }
}
```

[`DataAnchor`][data-anchor] maps a data-space point, line, or rectangle to its
item geometry. Its children (`Rectangle`, `Text`, `Canvas`, input handlers)
follow panning and zooming. Set matching X and/or Y coordinates for a point or
line; set all four bounds for a rectangle.

Each `DataAnchor` and its children add `QQuickItem`s, so use it for a moderate
number of rich annotations. For thousands of simple regions, use
[`RectangleSeries`][rectangle-series], which is a single item.

## Highlight many data regions

[`RectangleSeries`][rectangle-series] draws many data-space rectangles, such as
event windows or machine states. [`setData()`][rectangle-series-set-data] takes
rectangle bounds. An omitted or infinite edge reaches the plot edge, so
`{ x1: 8, x2: 12 }` is a full-height span:

```qml
QAccelPlot.RectangleSeries {
    xAxis: plot.xAxis
    yAxis: plot.yAxis
    color: "goldenrod"

    Component.onCompleted: setData([
        { x1: 8, x2: 12 },
        { x1: 19, x2: 22 }
    ])
}
```

Infinite edges don't change the axes' data ranges.

| Property | Use |
| :--- | :--- |
| `category`, `categoryColors` | Per-rectangle color: `category` indexes `categoryColors`; others use `color` |
| `minimumWidth`, `minimumHeight` | Minimum drawn size in pixels (default 1), so short events stay visible |
| `border.width`, `border.color` | Outline inside each rectangle, e.g. to separate adjacent states |
| `hoverColor` | Fill of the hovered rectangle |
| [`hoveredIndex`][hovered-index], `rectangleAt()` | The rectangle under the mouse pointer and its bounds, for tooltips |

A state timeline puts one lane per row, colored by category:

```qml
QAccelPlot.RectangleSeries {
    xAxis: plot.xAxis
    yAxis: plot.yAxis
    categoryColors: ["seagreen", "slategray", "firebrick"] // Running, Idle, Alarm
    border.width: 1

    Component.onCompleted: setData([
        { x1: 0, x2: 40, y1: -0.4, y2: 0.4, category: 0 },
        { x1: 40, x2: 43, y1: -0.4, y2: 0.4, category: 2 },
        { x1: 0, x2: 25, y1: 0.6, y2: 1.4, category: 1 }
    ])
}
```

Label the lanes with a [`TextTickLabelFormatter`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/axis-formats/#categories) on the
Y axis. From C++, `setData(std::vector<double>&&, std::vector<int>&&, int)`
moves bounds and categories in without copying; `postData()` hands them off
from a worker thread.

RectangleSeries only accepts hover over its rectangles, so series underneath
still receive hover elsewhere. Hover lookup uses a spatial grid, so it stays
fast for large collections unless many rectangles are very wide or tall; see
[Hover interactions](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/#hover-interactions).

## Build interactive tools

Plot mouse events carry pixel positions; convert them to data coordinates:

```qml
onMousePressed: event => {
    if (event.button === Qt.RightButton) {
        const dataX = pixelToDataX(event.x)
        const dataY = pixelToDataY(event.y)
        createToolAt(dataX, dataY)
        event.accept()
    }
}
```

Position handles with [`dataToPixelX()`][data-to-pixel-x] and
[`dataToPixelY()`][data-to-pixel-y]; convert drag positions back with
[`pixelToDataX()`][pixel-to-data-x] and [`pixelToDataY()`][pixel-to-data-y].
Call `event.accept()` when a tool handles an event so the gesture does not also
pan the plot or start rectangle zoom.

In a layer positioned at [`plotRect`][plot-rect], add or subtract the plot
rectangle origin to convert between plot and layer coordinates.

Complete sources:

- [`examples/interaction/annotations`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/interaction/annotations)
- [`examples/interaction/measurement_tools`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/interaction/measurement_tools)
- [`examples/plot_types/state_timeline`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/plot_types/state_timeline)

[plot-rect]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1QAccelPlot.md#property-plotrect-12
[data-to-pixel-x]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1QAccelPlot.md#function-datatopixelx
[data-to-pixel-y]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1QAccelPlot.md#function-datatopixely
[pixel-to-data-x]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1QAccelPlot.md#function-pixeltodatax
[pixel-to-data-y]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1QAccelPlot.md#function-pixeltodatay
[data-anchor]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1DataAnchor.md
[rectangle-series]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1RectangleSeries.md
[rectangle-series-set-data]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1RectangleSeries.md#function-setdata-18
[hovered-index]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1RectangleSeries.md#property-hoveredindex-12

<!-- source: docs/guide/cookbook/data-inspection.md -->

# Data inspection

`PlotInspector` shows a crosshair, a marker on every series, and a tooltip at
the cursor. `SelectionTool` selects a region and reports its statistics.

```qml
import QAccelPlot as QAccelPlot

QAccelPlot.Plot {
    id: plotView
    // Bind each series to its axes.
    QAccelPlot.PlotInspector {
        plot: plotView
        QAccelPlot.Crosshair { axisLabels: true }
        QAccelPlot.InspectionMarkers {}
        QAccelPlot.InspectionTooltip {}
    }
    QAccelPlot.SelectionTool { plot: plotView }
}
```

- Components declared inside a `PlotInspector` use it and are drawn in
  declaration order, the last one on top. A component declared elsewhere needs
  `inspector:` set and is not restacked.
- They are children of `plotView.overlay`, an item above the series and the
  legend. Parent your own overlays to it instead of choosing a `z` relative to
  the series.
- Shift + left drag selects a region; Escape clears it. Ordinary left dragging
  still pans.

[Rectangle zoom](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/rectangle-zoom/) defaults to Ctrl + left drag. If both are
set to the same gesture, `SelectionTool` takes it.

## Inspector

[`PlotInspector`][plot-inspector] queries every visible `LineCurve`,
`PointCloud`, and `HeatmapSeries` of the plot at the cursor. Other series types
have no row. A heatmap reports the cell under the cursor in every mode, at its
center; `radius`, `interpolate`, and `summaries` do not apply to it, and
`snapToDataPoint` moves both crosshair coordinates to the center.

| Property | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `mode` | `NearestX` reports each series at the cursor's X. `NearestY` does the same at the cursor's Y, for series whose independent variable is Y. `NearestXY` picks the data point closest on screen. |
| `radius` | Pick distance in logical pixels. In `NearestX` and `NearestY` it only applies beyond a series' extreme data points; between two data points a series always matches. |
| `interpolate` | In `NearestX` and `NearestY`, report the point on the line between two consecutive data points. On a step line it is on the step, and its `index` is the data point holding the value. |
| `snapToDataPoint` | Move the crosshair to the closest matching data point. |
| `summaries`, `summaryRadius` | Add the count and Y statistics of the data points within `summaryRadius` pixels of the cursor. Use it for dense data, where one pixel column holds many data points. |
| `includedSeries`, `excludedSeries` | Restrict the inspected series. |

The inspector reports `active`, `crosshairPosition` in plot-local pixels, the
cursor in data units (`cursorX`, `cursorY`, with their formatted texts) and in
pixels (`cursorPixelX`, `cursorPixelY`), `validCount`, and `model`.

### Tooltip rows

`inspector.model` has one row per inspected series, updated in place as the
cursor moves. Replace `InspectionTooltip.rowDelegate` to change a tooltip row,
and declare the roles it uses as required properties:

```qml
QAccelPlot.InspectionTooltip {
    rowDelegate: Text {
        required property bool valid
        required property string seriesName
        required property string yText
        visible: valid
        text: seriesName + " = " + yText
    }
}
```

[`InspectionRowModel`][row-model] lists the roles. Text roles such as `yText`
use the axis' tick formatter at a precision that follows the zoom level.
`valueText` holds the value of a heatmap cell or a colored `PointCloud` point
with up to six significant digits; the default row shows it after the
coordinates.

### Cursor from code

Set `followPointer: false` and write `cursorX`, `cursorY`, or both to place the
cursor in data coordinates. With one coordinate, series are matched along that
axis in every mode and heatmaps have no match. Link two plots by binding one
inspector to the other:

```qml
QAccelPlot.PlotInspector { id: top; plot: topPlot }
QAccelPlot.PlotInspector { plot: bottomPlot; followPointer: false; cursorX: top.cursorX }
```

To drive the cursor from a pixel position, such as a scripted pointer, write
`cursorPixelX` and `cursorPixelY` in plot-local pixels. The cursor stays on
those pixels when the axes pan or zoom, and `cursorX` and `cursorY` report the
data under it. A binding such as `cursorX: plot.pixelToDataX(x)` goes stale
instead, because `pixelToDataX()` has no change signal.

```qml
QAccelPlot.PlotInspector {
    plot: plotView
    followPointer: false
    cursorPixelX: pointer.x // pointer is in plot-local pixels
    cursorPixelY: pointer.y
}
```

Each coordinate is in the unit it was last written in: writing `cursorX` after
`cursorPixelX` places X in data units again.

One pixel can span several data points. To rest on a known data point, write
its `cursorX` and `cursorY` instead.

`stepCursor(n)` moves the cursor `n` source records along the first matching
XY series and stops following the mouse pointer; use it for keyboard
navigation.

## Queries

Every series exposes its queries as `series.inspection`. Call them on the series'
thread. Pixel arguments are series-local logical pixels: map a plot-local
position with `series.mapFromItem(plot, position)`.

```qml
const dataPoint = curve.inspection.nearestByX(curve.mapFromItem(plotView, plotView.pointerPosition).x)
if (dataPoint.valid)
    console.log(dataPoint.index, dataPoint.x, dataPoint.y)
```

| Query | Methods |
| --- | --- |
| A data point by index | `dataPointAt()` |
| Nearest valid data point | `nearest()`, `nearestByX()`, `nearestByY()` |
| Data points on either side and the point between them | `bracketByX()`, `bracketByY()` |
| Y statistics of a region or an X interval | `summarize()`, `summarizeRange()` |
| Source indices inside a region, in pages | `indices()` |
| Native record of a bar, rectangle, band, or heatmap series | `recordAt()`, `recordAtPosition()` |
| Heatmap cell at a position, as a data point | `dataPointAtPosition()` |

Results carry a `status` and a `valid` flag. Compare `status` with
`QAccelPlot.Inspection.Ready`, `NoMatch`, `Preparing`, or another status. A
query that does not apply to the series returns `Unsupported`.
[`SeriesInspection`][series-inspection] specifies regions, tie-breaking, and
paging.

### Readiness

| Data | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| X or Y finite and non-decreasing | Searched in place. No preparation and no index; `appendData()` keeps queries available. |
| Unordered, up to 20 000 records | Scanned per query. No preparation. |
| Unordered, more records | Indexed on a worker thread. Queries return `Preparing` until `inspection.status` is `Ready`; `statusChanged` announces it. |

- `nearestByX()`, `bracketByX()`, and their Y counterparts need the order along
  their own axis.
- `prepare()` starts indexing before the first query.
- Any data change discards the index. A stream that replaces unordered data
  faster than it can be indexed never becomes `Ready`.
- The index takes about 40 MB per million valid data points;
  `inspection.indexBytes()` reports the actual size.

## Selection

[`SelectionTool`][selection-tool] selects a `Box`, an `XRange`, or a `YRange`.
`button`, `modifiers`, and `minimumSize` configure the gesture; the modifiers
must match exactly and a shorter drag only clears the selection.

- The region is `xMin`, `xMax`, `yMin`, `yMax` in the coordinates of `xAxis` and
  `yAxis`, which default to the plot's primary axes. A range selection is
  unbounded in its other dimension.
- Visible XY series bound to the axis of every bounded dimension are selected,
  so an X range also covers series on a secondary Y axis.
- `model` has one row of statistics per selected series, recomputed when data
  changes. `indices(series, offset, limit)` pages through the selected data points.
- `select(xMin, xMax, yMin, yMax)` sets the region from code; `clear()` removes
  it. `selectionChanged` reports a new or cleared region, `completed` a
  finished gesture.
- Set `rectangleVisible: false` to draw `pixelRect` yourself.

Complete source: [`examples/interaction/data_inspection`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/interaction/data_inspection)

[plot-inspector]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1PlotInspector.md
[row-model]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1InspectionRowModel.md
[series-inspection]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1SeriesInspection.md
[selection-tool]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1SelectionTool.md

<!-- source: docs/guide/cookbook/point-clouds.md -->

# Point clouds

Use [`QAccelPlot.PointCloud`][point-cloud] for scatter data whose points are
not connected. It draws each point as a GPU marker and scales to hundreds of
thousands of points updated every frame. A `LineCurve` with `NoLine` and
markers suits small scatter plots only.

## Draw a scatter plot

```qml
QAccelPlot.Plot {
    id: plot
    xAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis { viewportMin: -10; viewportMax: 10 }
    yAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis { viewportMin: -8; viewportMax: 8 }

    QAccelPlot.PointCloud {
        id: samples
        name: "Samples"
        xAxis: plot.xAxis
        yAxis: plot.yAxis
        color: "#8065b5ff"
        marker.shape: QAccelPlot.PointCloud.Circle
        marker.size: 2

        Component.onCompleted: setData([Qt.point(-2, 1), Qt.point(3, 4), Qt.point(1, -3)])
    }
}
```

`marker` takes the same `shape`, `size`, `filled`, and `strokeWidth` as on a
`LineCurve`, except the shape `None`; see
[Marker shapes](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/styling/#marker-shapes).

Overlapping translucent markers blend separately, so dense regions read as
density. Points are drawn in data order.

The default legend shows the marker shape and `color`.

## Color points by value

Give each point a value and assign a [`Colormap`][colormap]:

```qml
QAccelPlot.PointCloud {
    xAxis: plot.xAxis
    yAxis: plot.yAxis
    colormap: QAccelPlot.Colormap { preset: QAccelPlot.Colormap.Viridis }
}
```

Without a colormap, or without per-point values, every point uses `color`.

The presets are `Viridis`, `Plasma`, `Inferno`, `Magma`, `Grayscale`, and
`Rainbow`; `reversed: true` runs a ramp from its last color to its first. For
a custom ramp, list `GradientStop`s in `stops`. The ramp follows bindings on
their `position` and `color`:

```qml
QAccelPlot.PointCloud {
    colormap: QAccelPlot.Colormap {
        stops: [
            GradientStop { position: 0.0; color: "#fde725" },
            GradientStop { position: 1.0; color: QAccelPlot.Colors.dark.seriesPrimary }
        ]
    }
}
```

`min` and `max` bound the value range. An unset bound is resolved from the
data, so series sharing one colormap can resolve different ranges.
`setRange(min, max)` sets both with one update. Set `norm` to `Colormap.Log`
when the values span decades; values at or below zero are then drawn with
`color`.

From QML, call `setValues()` after `setData()` with one value per point. From
C++, pass values together with the positions:

```cpp
cloud->setDataF(std::move(xyInterleaved), std::move(values), pointCount);
```

`setData()` takes the same arguments with a `std::vector<double>` of positions.
Values are single precision either way.

`dataValueMin` and `dataValueMax` expose the resolved bounds. Points with a
non-finite value use `color`.

## Show a color bar

[`QAccelPlot.ColorBar`][color-bar] draws the series' colormap with ticks for
the resolved value range:

```qml
QAccelPlot.Plot {
    id: plot

    QAccelPlot.PointCloud {
        id: cloud
        xAxis: plot.xAxis
        yAxis: plot.yAxis
        colormap: QAccelPlot.Colormap { preset: QAccelPlot.Colormap.Plasma }
    }

    QAccelPlot.ColorBar {
        series: cloud
        label: "Intensity"
        x: plot.plotRect.left + 8
        y: plot.plotRect.top + 8
    }
}
```

- The bar is an ordinary item: position it with `x`, `y`, or anchors. It does
  not reserve layout space, and the default legend sits at the top right of
  the plot area.
- The default bar is vertical, with its minimum at the bottom.
  `orientation: Qt.Horizontal` puts the minimum on the left.
- Set `height` on a vertical bar, or `width` on a horizontal one, to change its
  length. Raise `tickLabelWidth` when the labels of a vertical bar are clipped.
- `ticker` configures the ticks, as on `Axis.ticker`.
- `interactive: true` lets the user pan the range with a left drag, zoom it
  with the wheel, and resolve it from the data again with a double-click. The
  gestures set the colormap's `min` and `max`, so leave both unbound.

## Stream point data

From a worker thread, hand over complete frames with `postData()`, which
moves the buffers:

```cpp
// Worker thread
cloud->postData(std::move(xy), std::move(values), pointCount);
```

Post no faster than frames are presented; see
[Background data production](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/background-data/).

## Animate data changes

Assign a `MorphTransition` or a `DrawTransition` to `transition`, as for a
[`LineCurve`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/styling/#animated-data-changes).

- `MorphTransition` moves each point to the new position of the same index.
  Values change with it when the old and the new points both have them, so
  the colors blend through the colormap.
- `DrawTransition` shows the new points one after another.
- New points appear, and removed points disappear, at once.
- `count`, `pointAt()`, `valueAt()`, the data and value ranges, and inspection
  use the new data from the start of the animation. Hover picks the points as
  drawn.
- `setValues()` animates too. Called after `setData()`, it keeps that
  animation, with the points in their new colors.
- `clearData()` shows the new data at once.
- While a transition is enabled, the float paths store doubles.

## Invalid points

Non-finite coordinates, and non-positive ones on a logarithmic axis, are not
drawn, not picked, and do not contribute to axis data ranges. They stay in
storage, so indices are stable.

## Hover

`hoveredIndex` is the index of the valid point nearest to the mouse pointer
within `hoverRadius` pixels, or `-1`. Combine it with `pointAt()`, `valueAt()`,
and a `QAccelPlot.DataAnchor` to show a tooltip:

```qml
QAccelPlot.DataAnchor {
    readonly property point hovered: samples.hoveredIndex >= 0 ? samples.pointAt(samples.hoveredIndex) : Qt.point(0, 0)
    visible: samples.hoveredIndex >= 0
    xAxis: plot.xAxis
    yAxis: plot.yAxis
    plotRect: Qt.rect(0, 0, overlay.width, overlay.height)
    dataX1: hovered.x
    dataY1: hovered.y
    dataX2: hovered.x
    dataY2: hovered.y

    Text { text: "#" + samples.hoveredIndex }
}
```

Only positions near a point count as inside the series, so stacked series
underneath still receive hover events elsewhere. For the lookup cost, see
[Hover interactions](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/#hover-interactions).

## Limits

- `setData()` keeps doubles and uploads positions relative to an origin near
  the data, so values far from zero such as epoch timestamps stay precise.
  `setDataF()` stores floats.
- The number of drawable points is bounded by the GPU's maximum texture size:
  about 22 million points with values, or 33 million without, on a GPU with
  an 8192-pixel texture limit, and twice that with a 16384-pixel limit. Extra
  points are not drawn, and a warning is logged once.

Complete source: [`examples/plot_types/point_cloud`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/plot_types/point_cloud)

[point-cloud]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1PointCloud.md
[colormap]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1Colormap.md
[color-bar]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1ColorBar.md

<!-- source: docs/guide/cookbook/heatmaps.md -->

# Heatmaps

Use [`QAccelPlot.HeatmapSeries`][heatmap-series] for values sampled on a
regular grid, such as a field, an image, or a matrix. Each cell is colored by
its value through a [`Colormap`][colormap].

## Draw a heatmap

```qml
QAccelPlot.Plot {
    id: plot
    xAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis { viewportMin: -10; viewportMax: 10 }
    yAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis { viewportMin: -5; viewportMax: 5 }

    QAccelPlot.HeatmapSeries {
        xAxis: plot.xAxis
        yAxis: plot.yAxis
        xMin: -10; xMax: 10
        yMin: -5; yMax: 5
        // Three columns by two rows.
        Component.onCompleted: setValues([0, 1, 2,
                                          3, 4, 5], 3)
    }
}
```

- Values are stored row by row, `columns` per row. Row 0 is at `yMin` and
  column 0 at `xMin`.
- `xMin`, `xMax`, `yMin`, and `yMax` are the outer edges of the grid, so a
  cell is `(xMax - xMin) / columns` wide. An unset edge places the grid in
  index space: column `c` spans `[c, c + 1]`. A reversed extent flips the grid.
- The grid edges are the series' data range, so `rescaleToData()` fits the
  whole grid.
- `setValues()` sets `columns`. Do not bind `columns` while using it: when
  the binding is re-evaluated, it reshapes the grid.
- `valueAt(row, column)` reads a cell.

## Use logarithmic axes and spacing

`xSpacing` and `ySpacing` set how cells are spaced between the grid edges,
independently of the axis scale:

- `HeatmapSeries.Linear` (default): cells of equal size in data coordinates.
- `HeatmapSeries.Log`: cells of equal size in log10, each spanning the same
  ratio, such as constant-Q or octave bins.

| Spacing | Linear axis | Log axis |
|---|---|---|
| `Linear` | Equal widths | Narrower toward larger values |
| `Log` | Wider toward larger values | Equal widths |

```qml
QAccelPlot.Plot {
    id: plot
    yAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis { viewportMin: 20; viewportMax: 20000; logScale: true }

    QAccelPlot.HeatmapSeries {
        xAxis: plot.xAxis
        yAxis: plot.yAxis
        xMin: 0; xMax: 10
        // Rows of equal frequency ratio from 20 Hz to 20 kHz.
        yMin: 20; yMax: 20000
        ySpacing: QAccelPlot.HeatmapSeries.Log
    }
}
```

- On a log axis, the parts of `Linear` cells at or below zero are not drawn,
  and the data range starts at the first cell edge above zero. A grid from
  0 Hz, such as FFT bins, keeps its first bin.
- `Log` spacing needs both edges of that dimension positive. Set them: an
  unset edge resolves to index space, which starts at 0. Otherwise the series
  draws nothing, reports no data range in that dimension, and logs a warning.

## Choose the colors

The series starts with its own Viridis `Colormap`, with the value range
resolved from the data. Change it in place, or assign a shared one:

```qml
QAccelPlot.HeatmapSeries {
    colormap: QAccelPlot.Colormap {
        preset: QAccelPlot.Colormap.Inferno
        min: -1
        max: 1
    }
}
```

The colormap works as for [point clouds](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/point-clouds/#color-points-by-value):
presets, `reversed`, custom `stops`, fixed or data-resolved `min` and `max`,
and `norm: Colormap.Log`. `dataValueMin` and `dataValueMax` expose the resolved
range. Nothing is drawn while `colormap` is null.

These cells are transparent:

- cells with a non-finite value, such as `NaN` for missing data;
- under a `Log` colormap, cells with a value at or below zero.

Non-finite values do not count toward the value range.

## Show a color bar

A [`ColorBar`][color-bar] keys a heatmap as it keys a point cloud; see
[Show a color bar](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/point-clouds/#show-a-color-bar):

```qml
QAccelPlot.ColorBar {
    series: heatmap
    label: "Amplitude"
    interactive: true
}
```

A heatmap has no legend entry: the color bar is its key. A histogram of the
values can key it instead; see
[Use a histogram as a color bar](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/histograms/#use-a-histogram-as-a-color-bar).

## Read the cell under the pointer

A [`PlotInspector`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/data-inspection/#inspector) reports the cell under the
cursor in every mode. Its row has the cell center (geometric under `Log`
spacing) as `dataPointX` and `dataPointY`, the value as `dataPointValue` and
`valueText`, and `row * columns + column` as `dataPointIndex`.
`InspectionTooltip` shows the center and the value:

```qml
QAccelPlot.PlotInspector {
    plot: plot

    QAccelPlot.InspectionTooltip {}
}
```

A cell with a non-finite value is still a match. In code,
`inspection.dataPointAtPosition()` returns the same data point for a
series-local position: pixels from the top left of the plot area.
`inspection.recordAtPosition()` and `inspection.recordAt(index)` return the
cell's record, whose `fields` are `x` and `y` (the cell center), `value`,
`row`, and `column`. While a grid edge is infinite, or not positive under
`Log` spacing, `recordAt()` returns `Inspection.Unavailable` and no position
matches a cell.

## Set data from C++

`setValues()` replaces the values and the shape together:

```cpp
// columns * rows floats, row by row.
heatmap->setValues(std::move(values), columns, rows);
```

From a worker thread, `postValues()` takes the same arguments and queues the
handoff; see [Background data production](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/background-data/).

The `PlotSeries` setters, such as `setDataF(std::move(values), count)` and
`postData()`, take one value per cell and keep `columns`, so `count` must be
a multiple of it. Setting `columns` keeps the values and recomputes `rows`.

## Limits

- Each pixel takes the color of the cell under its center. Cells are not
  interpolated.
- Values are single precision.
- A grid with an infinite edge, such as `xMin: -Infinity`, draws nothing.
- A grid can have as many cells as the GPU data texture holds: about 67
  million on a GPU with an 8192-pixel texture limit. A larger grid is not
  drawn, and a warning is logged.
- A grid of more than 16,777,216 (2^24) columns or rows is not drawn, and a
  warning is logged: the GPU locates cells in single precision.

Complete source: [`examples/plot_types/heatmap`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/plot_types/heatmap)

[heatmap-series]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1HeatmapSeries.md
[colormap]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1Colormap.md
[color-bar]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1ColorBar.md

<!-- source: docs/guide/cookbook/rectangle-zoom.md -->

# Rectangle zoom

Rectangle zoom is disabled by default. Enable it on `Plot` or `PlotView`:

```qml
import QAccelPlot as QAccelPlot

QAccelPlot.Plot {
    rectangleZoom.enabled: true
}
```

- Ctrl + left drag (Command on macOS) selects a region; release to zoom all
  attached axes.
- Escape cancels. Double-click rescales to the data. Ordinary left dragging pans.
- The selection is clipped to the plot area and must be at least
  `rectangleZoom.minimumSize` logical pixels wide and high, 6 by default.
- `rectangleZoom.modifiers` must match exactly at press time; use
  `Qt.NoModifier` for unmodified dragging. A
  [`SelectionTool`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/data-inspection/#selection) uses Shift + left drag by
  default; if both are set to the same gesture, the `SelectionTool` takes it.
- `rectangleZoom.fillColor` and `borderColor` default to the dark palette's
  `rectangleZoomFill` and `rectangleZoomBorder`. Bind them to `Colors.light`
  for a light theme.

For a custom tool, call [`zoomToRect()`][zoom-to-rect] with item-local pixels:

```qml
const applied = plot.zoomToRect(Qt.rect(left, top, width, height))
```

It works with gestures disabled and supports logarithmic and reversed axes.
It returns `false` without changing ranges if the selection or target axes are invalid.

Complete source: [`examples/plot_types/point_cloud`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/plot_types/point_cloud)

[zoom-to-rect]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1QAccelPlot.md#function-zoomtorect
