<!-- source: docs/guide/cookbook/bar-charts.md -->

# Bar charts

Use [`QAccelPlot.BarSeries`][bar-series] for bar charts. Each bar is a
(position, value) pair. Changing `barWidth`, `barOffset`, or `baselineValue`
does not re-upload the data.

## Draw bars

```qml
QAccelPlot.Plot {
    id: plot
    xAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis { viewportMin: -0.5; viewportMax: 3.5 }
    yAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis { viewportMin: 0; viewportMax: 10 }

    QAccelPlot.BarSeries {
        name: "Sales"
        xAxis: plot.xAxis
        yAxis: plot.yAxis
        Component.onCompleted: setData([4, 7, 5, 9])
    }
}
```

`setData()` takes numbers, placed at positions 0, 1, 2, …, or objects with
`position`, `value`, and an optional `category`:

```qml
setData([{ position: 2020, value: 4 }, { position: 2021, value: 7 }])
```

| Property | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `barWidth` | 0.8 | Bar width in position-axis data units |
| `barOffset` | 0 | Shift of every bar along the position axis |
| `baselineValue` | 0 | Value the bars start from |
| `minimumWidth` | 1 | Minimum drawn width in pixels |
| `orientation` | `Qt.Vertical` | `Qt.Horizontal` puts positions on the Y axis |

Values below `baselineValue` extend the bar the other way. Set
`baselineValue: -Infinity` to start the bars at the plot edge. On a
logarithmic value axis, a baseline at or below zero also starts at the plot
edge.

For category labels, use a [`TextTickLabelFormatter`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/axis-formats/) on the
position axis.

## Group bars

Use one series per group member. Split the group width between them and
offset each by its index:

```qml
Repeater {
    model: ["North", "South", "West"]

    QAccelPlot.BarSeries {
        required property int index
        required property string modelData

        name: modelData
        xAxis: plot.xAxis
        yAxis: plot.yAxis
        barWidth: 0.8 / 3
        barOffset: (index - 1) * barWidth
        Component.onCompleted: setData(revenue[index])
    }
}
```

## Give bars their own extent

A ranged bar spans from `from` to `to` along the position axis instead of
being centered on a position:

```qml
setData([{ from: 0, to: 1, value: 4 }, { from: 1, to: 5, value: 7 }])
```

`barWidth` and `barOffset` do not apply to ranged bars. A series holds either
ranged bars or position bars: when any object has `from` or `to`, all of them
are ranged. [Histograms](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/histograms/) are drawn this way.

## Color bars by category

Give bars a `category` and list the colors in `categoryColors`. Bars without a
category, or with one outside the list, use `color`.

```qml
QAccelPlot.BarSeries {
    categoryColors: ["#4ade80", "#f87171"]
    Component.onCompleted: setData(profit.map((value, month) => ({
        position: month,
        value: value,
        category: value >= 0 ? 0 : 1
    })))
}
```

`setCategories()` replaces the categories without changing the data. Outlines
are set with `border.width` and `border.color`.

## Color bars by value

Assign a [`Colormap`][colormap] to color each bar from `colorSource`:

```qml
QAccelPlot.BarSeries {
    colorSource: QAccelPlot.BarSeries.Position
    colormap: QAccelPlot.Colormap {
        preset: QAccelPlot.Colormap.Viridis
        min: 0
        max: 10
    }
}
```

| `colorSource` | Mapped to a color |
| --- | --- |
| `BarSeries.Value` (default) | The bar's value |
| `BarSeries.Position` | The bar's position; for a ranged bar, the middle of its edges under the colormap's `norm` |

- The colormap overrides `color` and `categoryColors`; `hoverColor` still
  marks the hovered bar.
- `min` and `max` work as for [point clouds](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/point-clouds/#color-points-by-value).
  An unset bound resolves from the data, and ranged bars contribute both edges.
  `dataValueMin` and `dataValueMax` expose the resolved range.
- Values outside the range take the color at its nearer end.
- `barOffset` does not move a bar's position on the colormap.
- Under `norm: Colormap.Log`, a bar at or below zero keeps `color` or its
  category color. If an unset bound resolves from such a bar, the range is not
  positive and every bar keeps its color; set `min` above zero.
- A [`ColorBar`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/point-clouds/#show-a-color-bar) keys the series. To key a
  heatmap with a histogram of its values instead, see
  [Use a histogram as a color bar](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/histograms/#use-a-histogram-as-a-color-bar).

## Hover

`hoveredIndex` is the bar under the mouse pointer, or -1. `barAt(index)`
returns its `position`, `value`, and `category`; a ranged bar has `from` and
`to` instead of `position`. Set `hoverColor` to highlight it.
`minimumWidth` also widens the hover area.

## Animate data changes

Assign a `MorphTransition` or a `DrawTransition` to `transition`, as for a
[`LineCurve`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/styling/#animated-data-changes).

- `MorphTransition` moves each bar to its new position and value. New bars
  grow from `baselineValue`, and removed bars shrink to it.
- `DrawTransition` shows the new bars one after another.
- `count`, `barAt()`, the data ranges, hover, and inspection use the new data
  from the start of the animation.
- `clearData()` shows the new data at once.
- While a transition is enabled, the float paths store doubles.

## Feed data from C++

Pass a vector of interleaved `(position, value)` pairs to `setData()`:

```cpp
// Three bars: 4 at position 0, 7 at position 1, 5 at position 2.
auto data = std::vector<double>{0.0, 4.0, 1.0, 7.0, 2.0, 5.0};
bars->setData(std::move(data), 3);
```

`setData()` keeps doubles and uploads them relative to an origin near the
data, so large positions such as epoch timestamps stay precise.

Ranged bars are interleaved `(from, to, value)` triples passed to
`setRangedData()`, or to `postRangedData()` from a worker thread.

For the highest throughput, use `setDataF()`, or `postData()` from a worker
thread; see the
[Performance guide](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/).

## Invalid bars

A bar with a NaN or infinite position, or a NaN value, is not drawn. An
infinite value reaches the plot edge.

Complete source: [`examples/plot_types/bar_chart`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/plot_types/bar_chart)

[bar-series]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1BarSeries.md
[colormap]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1Colormap.md

<!-- source: docs/guide/cookbook/histograms.md -->

# Histograms

[`Histogram`][histogram] counts samples into bins and returns one bar per bin
for a [`BarSeries`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/bar-charts/).

## Count samples

```qml
QAccelPlot.BarSeries {
    xAxis: plot.xAxis
    yAxis: plot.yAxis

    Component.onCompleted: setData(QAccelPlot.Histogram.fromSamples(samples, 40).bars())
}
```

`fromSamples(samples, 40)` spreads 40 bins over the samples.
`fromSamples(samples, 40, -3, 3)` uses a fixed range instead.

## Choose the bin edges

Pass bin edges instead of a bin count:

```qml
const edges = QAccelPlot.Histogram.logEdges(1, 10000, 40);
setData(QAccelPlot.Histogram.fromSamples(samples, edges).bars());
```

| Edges | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `[0, 1, 2, 5, 10]` | Any list of finite, strictly increasing numbers |
| `Histogram.linearEdges(0, 10, 20)` | 20 equal bins from 0 to 10 |
| `Histogram.logEdges(1, 10000, 40)` | 40 bins of equal width on a logarithmic axis |
| `Histogram.decadeEdges(1, 10000)` | One bin between each pair of logarithmic axis ticks: 1, 2, …, 9, 10, 20, … |

The bars are [ranged](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/bar-charts/#give-bars-their-own-extent): each one spans
its bin, whatever its width. `orientation: Qt.Horizontal` on the series puts
the bins on the Y axis.

## Density

`density()` divides each count by the sample count and the bin width, so the
bin areas sum to 1:

```qml
setData(QAccelPlot.Histogram.fromSamples(samples, edges).density().bars());
```

Use it when bins differ in width, or to compare data sets of different sizes.
A wide bin collects more samples than a narrow one, so raw counts of uneven
bins misrepresent the distribution.

On a logarithmic axis, `logEdges()` bins have equal drawn widths, so their raw
counts show the shape of the distribution. `decadeEdges()` bins widen tenfold
at each power of ten, so draw them as density.

## Counting rules

| Sample | Counted in |
| --- | --- |
| On an edge | The bin above it; the last bin includes its upper edge |
| NaN, or outside the edges | No bin |

Invalid edges or a bin count below 1 give an empty histogram (`binCount` 0)
and a logged warning. A histogram exposes `binCount`, `edges`, `values`,
`total`, `uniform`, and `binWidth`, which is NaN for uneven bins.

## C++

```cpp
#include <QAccelPlot/data/Histogram.hpp>

using QAccelPlot::Histogram;

const auto histogram = Histogram::fromSamples(samples.data(), samples.size(), 40);
bars->setRangedData(histogram.barData(), histogram.binCount());

const auto density = Histogram::fromSamples(samples.data(), samples.size(), Histogram::logEdges(1.0, 10000.0, 40)).density();
bars->setRangedData(density.barData(), density.binCount());
```

`samples` is an array of `double` or `float`. The functions keep no state, so
a worker thread can build the histogram and pass its data to
`postRangedData()`.
`Histogram::fromCounts(edges, counts)` wraps data that is already binned.

## Use a histogram as a color bar

A histogram of a heatmap's values can key its colors: color the bins with the
heatmap's colormap through
[`colorSource: BarSeries.Position`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/bar-charts/#color-bars-by-value), and let
the histogram's bin axis set the colormap range. With horizontal bars, that is
`yAxis`, the bars' position axis:

```qml
QAccelPlot.Colormap {
    id: amplitudeColors
    min: histogramPlot.yAxis.viewportMin
    max: histogramPlot.yAxis.viewportMax
}

QAccelPlot.HeatmapSeries {
    colormap: amplitudeColors
}

QAccelPlot.Plot {
    id: histogramPlot
    xAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis { autoRescale: true }
    yAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis {}

    QAccelPlot.BarSeries {
        xAxis: histogramPlot.xAxis
        yAxis: histogramPlot.yAxis
        orientation: Qt.Horizontal
        colorSource: QAccelPlot.BarSeries.Position
        colormap: amplitudeColors
    }
}
```

- Panning or zooming the bin axis recolors the heatmap and the bins.
- Fill the bars with `setRangedData()`, and call `rescaleToData()` on the
  bin axis once to fit it to the bin edges.
- Keep the bin edges fixed when recounting, for example over the cells in
  view, so the bin axis is never refitted under the user.

The Interference page of
[`examples/plot_types/heatmap`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/plot_types/heatmap)
recounts the cells in view as the heatmap pans and zooms.

Complete source: [`examples/plot_types/histogram`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/plot_types/histogram)

[histogram]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1Histogram.md


---

<!-- source: docs/guide/cookbook/bands.md -->

# Bands

Use [`QAccelPlot.BandSeries`][band-series] to fill the area between a low and a
high value at each X: confidence and prediction intervals, tolerance masks, and
min/max or mean ± σ envelopes. Draw the center line with a separate
`LineCurve`.

Panning and zooming a band costs nothing on the CPU, whatever its size. Dashed
edge lines are the exception: zooming recomputes their dash positions in one
pass over the data points.

## Draw a band around a line

```qml
QAccelPlot.Plot {
    id: plot
    xAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis { viewportMin: 0; viewportMax: 10 }
    yAxis: QAccelPlot.Axis { viewportMin: 0; viewportMax: 10 }

    QAccelPlot.BandSeries {
        name: "90% interval"
        xAxis: plot.xAxis
        yAxis: plot.yAxis
        color: "#4065b5ff"
        Component.onCompleted: setData([0, 5, 10], [2, 4, 3], [4, 7, 8])
    }

    QAccelPlot.LineCurve {
        name: "Forecast"
        xAxis: plot.xAxis
        yAxis: plot.yAxis
        color: "#65b5ff"
        Component.onCompleted: setData([Qt.point(0, 3), Qt.point(5, 5.5), Qt.point(10, 5.5)])
    }
}
```

Declare the band before the line so the line is drawn on top. Nested intervals
are separate bands, widest first.

At each data point the band spans from the smaller to the larger of `low` and
`high`, so swapped values still fill correctly.

The default legend shows a `Fill` swatch in the band's `color`.

## Edge lines

Set `edges.width` to draw lines along the lower and upper edges:

```qml
QAccelPlot.BandSeries {
    edges.width: 1
    edges.color: "#b065b5ff"
    edges.lineStyle: QAccelPlot.DashLine { pattern: [4, 3] }
}
```

| Property | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `edges.width` | `0` | No edge lines at 0. |
| `edges.color` | invalid | Uses the band's `color` at full opacity. |
| `edges.lineStyle` | `SolidLine` | `DashLine` and `NoLine` also work. |

## Feed data from C++

Data points are interleaved `(x, low, high)` triples. The data API matches
`LineCurve` with three values per data point:

```cpp
auto dataPoints = std::vector<double>{};
dataPoints.reserve(count * 3);
for (auto i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
    dataPoints.insert(dataPoints.end(), {x[i], mean[i] - 2 * sigma[i], mean[i] + 2 * sigma[i]});
}
band->setData(std::move(dataPoints), count);
```

For float buffers, worker-thread handoff, and data bounds, see
[Select the data path](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/#select-the-data-path).

- `setData()` keeps doubles and uploads them relative to an origin near the
  viewport, so epoch timestamps stay precise. `setDataF()` stores floats.
- `postData()` hands a buffer over from any thread without copying it.
- `setData(xs, lows, highs)` takes three separate arrays, from QML or C++.
- `appendData(x, low, high)` adds one data point.

## Invalid data points

A data point is invalid when `x`, `low`, or `high` is `NaN` or `±Inf`, or is not
strictly positive on a logarithmic axis. The fill and the edge lines leave a
gap there. Auto-ranging skips invalid values one by one.

## Hover

`hovered` is `true` while the mouse pointer is inside the band or on an edge
line. Only the topmost series under the mouse pointer is hovered, so nested
bands highlight one at a time. Set `hoverEnabled: false` on a series drawn over
a band to leave hover to the band:

```qml
QAccelPlot.BandSeries {
    color: hovered ? "#8065b5ff" : "#4065b5ff"
    edges.width: hovered ? 1 : 0
}
```

## Limits

At most 16,777,216 (2^24) data points are drawn, fewer on GPUs whose maximum
texture size is below 6144. Data points beyond the limit are not drawn or
hovered, and a warning is logged once.

Complete source: [`examples/plot_types/bands`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/plot_types/bands)

[band-series]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1BandSeries.md


---

<!-- source: docs/guide/cookbook/background-data.md -->

# Background data production

Produce large or expensive buffers off the UI thread and hand over only
completed buffers.

## Simplest handoff

[`LineCurve::postData()`][post-data] can be called from any thread. It moves
the buffer into a queued call that runs [`setDataF()`][set-data-f] on the
curve's thread:

```cpp
void Producer::publish(QAccelPlot::LineCurve* curve)
{
    auto points = buildInterleavedPoints();
    const auto count = static_cast<int>(points.size() / 2);
    curve->postData(std::move(points), count);
}
```

## One-batch handoff

For high-rate updates, keep one pending batch. The worker prepares the next
batch and waits until the UI thread has consumed the previous one. Once per
frame, the UI thread moves the pending batch into the curve. This bounds memory
and skips frames that could never be displayed.

```cpp
DataBatch batch;
if (worker.tryConsume(batch)) {
    curve->setDataF(std::move(batch.points), batch.pointCount);
}
```

If the worker already knows the extents, add them to the batch and pass them
as `DataBounds` to skip the
[range scan](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/#data-ranges-are-computed-on-demand) on the UI
thread.

The performance showcase also builds the vertex cache on the worker. Adopt that
only after profiling the simpler handoff.

Complete source: [`examples/showcases/performance`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/showcases/performance)

[post-data]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1LineCurve.md#function-postdata-22
[set-data-f]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1LineCurve.md#function-setdataf-26


---

<!-- source: docs/guide/cookbook/export.md -->

# Exporting images

[`PlotExporter`][plot-exporter] captures a plot as a raster image:

```qml
import QAccelPlot as QAccelPlot

QAccelPlot.PlotExporter {
    id: exporter
    plot: plot
    scale: 2
    onFinished: (ok, path, error) => console.log(ok ? "Saved " + path : error)
}

Button {
    text: "Save"
    enabled: !exporter.busy
    onClicked: exporter.save("plot.png")
}
```

| Method | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `save(path)` | Writes a file in the format the suffix names. `path` may be a `file:` URL from a `FileDialog`. |
| `copyToClipboard()` | Puts the image on the clipboard. |
| `grabImage()` | Emits `imageReady(image)` with a `QImage`. |
| `supportedFormats()` | Lists the suffixes `save()` accepts, such as `png`, `jpg`, `bmp`, `webp`, `tif`. Image format plugins decide which are present. |

The image contains the plot item and everything inside its bounds as shown on
screen: series, axes, the legend, overlays, and child items.

## Options

| Property | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scale` | `0` | Image pixels per logical pixel. `0` uses the window's device pixel ratio, so the image matches the screen. The layout does not change: a 2× image has the same ticks and text positions, drawn at twice the resolution. At a device pixel ratio other than 1, a side can differ by one pixel from its size × scale. |
| `quality` | `-1` | 0–100, passed to `QImageWriter`. `-1` uses the format's default. JPEG and WebP trade size for artifacts; PNG stays lossless. |
| `dpi` | `0` | Resolution stored in the file. `0` stores 96 × scale, so documents place the image at its on-screen size. |
| `transparentBackground` | `false` | Leaves out `axesAreaColor` and `plotAreaColor`, so the image takes the background it is placed on. The grid, series, axes, and legend are drawn as usual. |

Formats without an alpha channel, such as JPEG and BMP, composite transparent
pixels over white. For a light image of a dark-themed plot, bind its colors to
`Colors.light` before exporting, as the
[Theming example](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/styling/theming)
does.

## Requests

- Each request ends with one `finished(ok, path, error)`. `path` is empty
  except for `save()`.
- A request made while `busy` only returns `false` and warns; `finished()`
  stays with the request in progress.
- The capture happens on the next frame. It fails if the window is hidden,
  minimized, or destroyed first. Encoding and writing the file run on a worker
  thread, and an existing file is replaced only once the new one is complete.
- A request fails immediately, returning `false`, when another exporter is
  capturing the same plot, the file format is unsupported, the plot is hidden,
  has no size, or is not in a window, the window is hidden or minimized, the
  window uses the software backend, or the image would exceed the GPU's
  maximum texture size.
- With `transparentBackground` set, the plot shows no background for the one
  frame the capture is taken in.

## C++

```cpp
auto* exporter = new QAccelPlot::PlotExporter(this);
exporter->setPlot(plot);
exporter->setScale(3.0);
connect(exporter, &QAccelPlot::PlotExporter::imageReady, this, [](const QImage& image) {
    // Use the image on the UI thread.
});
exporter->grabImage();
```

Complete source: [`examples/data/export`](https://github.com/michalgrabarczyk/QAccelPlot/tree/main/examples/data/export)

[plot-exporter]: ../api/classQAccelPlot_1_1PlotExporter.md

# API reference

- [Class list](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/annotated/)
- [Class index](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classes/)
- [Class hierarchy](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/hierarchy/)
- [Namespaces](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/namespaces/)
- [Files](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/files/)

## Key types

- [`PlotView`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1QAccelPlot/) — plot item: layout,
  pan and zoom, coordinate conversion, grid, and series collection. QML
  applications use its `Plot` wrapper.
- [`Axis`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1Axis/) — ranges, log scale, ticks, labels,
  and per-axis pan and zoom.
- [`PlotRectangleZoom`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1PlotRectangleZoom/) — gesture
  configuration, selection styling, and read-only selection state.
- [`LineCurve`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1LineCurve/) — GPU-rendered lines and
  markers, data ingestion, effects, transitions, gaps, and hover.
- [`PointCloud`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1PointCloud/) — large sets of
  unconnected points as markers, colored uniformly or by per-point values.
- [`HeatmapSeries`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1HeatmapSeries/) — a uniform
  grid of values as cells colored through a colormap.
- [`ColorBar`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1ColorBar/) — continuous key for the
  colormap and value range of a point cloud or heatmap.
- [`BandSeries`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1BandSeries/) — filled area between a
  low and a high value at each X, with optional edge lines.
- [`ErrorBarSeries`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1ErrorBarSeries/) — capped lines
  from a low to a high bound at each data point, vertical or horizontal.
- [`RectangleSeries`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1RectangleSeries/) — many data-space
  rectangles in one item: spans and state timelines.
- [`BarSeries`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1BarSeries/) — vertical, horizontal, and
  grouped bar charts, and ranged bars such as histogram bins.
- [`Histogram`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1Histogram/) — samples counted into
  bins, as data for a `BarSeries`.
- [`DataAnchor`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1DataAnchor/) — QML overlays at data
  coordinates.
- [`PlotMouseEvent`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1PlotMouseEvent/) — mouse
  positions in plot and data coordinates.
- [`LegendModel`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1LegendModel/) — legend entries of the
  visible series that have one, each a [`LegendEntry`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/structQAccelPlot_1_1LegendEntry/).
- [`SeriesInspection`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1SeriesInspection/) — per-series
  data queries: nearest data points, brackets, region statistics, and index pages.
- [`PlotInspector`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1PlotInspector/) — cursor state and
  one model row per series for crosshairs and tooltips.
- [`SelectionTool`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1SelectionTool/) — data-space box
  and range selection with per-series statistics.

See [Data inspection](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/cookbook/data-inspection/) for usage and readiness.

## Feeding curve data

- `setData()` — QML data or double-precision C++ containers.
- `setDataF(std::vector<float>&&, count)` — large interleaved buffers on the
  curve's thread.
- [`postData()`](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/api/classQAccelPlot_1_1LineCurve/#function-postdata-22) —
  completed buffers from a worker thread.
- `PlotSeries::DataBounds` — passed with the data when its extents are already known.
- `NaN` marks a missing data point; `gaps.nanMode` breaks or connects the curve.
  See [Invalid data points and gaps](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/concepts/#invalid-data-points-and-gaps).

See [Select the data path](https://michalgrabarczyk.github.io/QAccelPlot/performance/#select-the-data-path).
